yttrotantalite: A tantalate of uranium, yttrium, and calcium, of a brown or black color.
yttriferous: Bearing or containing yttrium or the allied elements; as, gadolinite is one of the yttriferous minerals.
ytterbic: Pertaining to, or derived from, ytterbium; containing ytterbium.
yttria: The oxide, Y2O3, or earth, of yttrium.
yttrocolumbite: A tantalate of uranium, yttrium, and calcium, of a brown or black color.
yt: , an old method of printing that (AS. æt, edhæt) the "y" taking the place of the old letter "Þ"). Cf. Ye, the. | an old method of printing that (AS. þæt, ðæt) the "y" taking the place of the old letter "thorn" (þ). Cf. Ye, the.
yttric: Pertaining to, derived from, or containing, yttrium.
yttrium: A rare metallic element of the boron-aluminium group, found in gadolinite and other rare minerals, and extracted as a dark gray powder. Symbol Y. Atomic weight, 89. [Written also ittrium.] Note: Associated with yttrium are certain rare elements, as erbium, ytterbium, samarium, etc., which are separated in a pure state with great difficulty.
ytterbium: A rare element of the boron group, sometimes associated with yttrium or other related elements, as in euxenite and gadolinite. Symbol Yb; provisional atomic weight 173.2. Cf. Yttrium. Note: Ytterbium is associated with other rare elements, and probably has not been prepared in a pure state.
yttrocerite: A mineral of a violet-blue color, inclining to gray and white. It is a hydrous fluoride of cerium, yttrium, and calcium.
